tookIdeas: the shape of the toolkit: an NSS fit, full revaluation by bump and reprice for effective duration and convexity, key-rate duration tents, a shock library, seeded risk numbers
that duration and convexity are measured by repricing, not by closed-form modified duration
notTaken: any code (Python, numpy, scipy; nothing was copied or translated line by line)
the curve model: yield-curve-sim treats the par curve as the zero curve (curve.py discount); this package bootstraps par yields to zero rates
the live Treasury CSV fetch (this package has no I/O)
the PCA shock and the VaR/ES simulation (not in this release)
inspirations.knownFlaw: Reads par yields as zero rates (stated in its own docstring). Not repeated: bootstrap.js, with a test that the shortcut gives a different discount factor on a sloped curve.

tookIdeas: which formulas an SA-CCR and an SMA calculator need and how they chain (add-on, multiplier, EAD; BI, BIC, ILM, capital)
the multiplier and EAD expressions as a cross-check of the standard's text
notTaken: any code (MATLAB with a Java jar; nothing was copied or translated)

its SMA calibration: BaselOP.m implements the 2016 consultative SMA (buckets 11/15/19/23% at 1/3/10/30bn, ILM = ln(1.7183 + LC/BIC)); this package implements the final standard (OPE25: 12/15/18% at 1bn and 30bn, ILM = ln(e - 1 + (LC/BIC)^0.8))
inspirations.knownFlaw: The SMA of the 2016 consultation is superseded by the final standard (BCBS d424, OPE25).

tookIdeas: rule-driven double-entry with Decimal money as the architecture for a later bank-day ledger engine (not in this release)
notTaken: its capital ratio (equity over total assets, no risk weights)

standards.title: Interest rate risk in the banking book (Basel Framework SRP31; BCBS d368, April 2016)
standards.note: Consolidated text of 2019-12-15. Worked examples of SRP31.92 are the fixtures.

standards.title: Standardised approach to counterparty credit risk, SA-CCR (Basel Framework CRE52; BCBS 279, March 2014, rev. April 2014)
standards.note: Formulas are images in the published HTML; the text of the paragraphs and Table 2 were read, the formulas are cross-checked against the worked examples.

standards.title: Illustrative examples of the SA-CCR (Basel Framework CRE99; BCBS 279 Annex 4)
standards.note: Worked examples 1 to 5 are the fixtures (intermediate figures as printed; final EADs by recomputation, their formula images are not in the HTML text).

standards.title: Operational risk, standardised approach (Basel Framework OPE25 and OPE10; BCBS d424, December 2017)
standards.note: The EUR 35bn example of OPE25.7 fn 2 is the fixture. The final calibration (12/15/18%) is implemented, not the 2016 consultation.

standards.title: Liquidity Coverage Ratio (Basel Framework LCR20, LCR30, LCR40; BCBS d238, January 2013)
standards.note: The standard publishes no numeric LCR case besides the deposit-insurance split of LCR40.7 fn 43; caps are validated by their defining inequalities.

standards.title: Net Stable Funding Ratio (Basel Framework NSF20, NSF30; BCBS d295, October 2014)
standards.note: No published numeric NSFR example was found; validated by hand computation and an independent copy of the factor table.
